0.0.n: Introduces the first feature the speaker will discuss.

0.1.n: Part of the feature name カメラコントロール, Camera Control.

0.2.n: Completes the feature name カメラコントロール, borrowed from English.

0.4.n: こっち is a casual way to indicate this direction; 側 adds the idea of a side.

0.5.n: Links this side to the power button mentioned next, with ね inserted as a conversational pause.

0.6.n: Adds a conversational pause while directing the listener's attention.

0.8.n: Combines with ボタン to identify the device's power button.

0.9.n: Together with 電源, names the button used to switch power on or off.

0.10.n: Links the power button to 横, identifying what the new button is beside.

0.11.n: Used with の and に to describe a position next to something.

0.12.n: Marks the location where the button exists.

0.13.n: Points to a nearby item and must come before a noun.

0.14.n: Refers to the Camera Control button being shown.

0.15.n: Identifies this button as the thing that exists in the stated location.

0.16.n: Polite connecting form of ある, leaving the sentence open for the explanation that follows.

1.0.n: Refers to the button; the object marker を is omitted in casual speech.

1.1.n: Plain form of 押す, followed by こと to treat pressing as an action.

1.2.n: Turns 押す into a noun-like phrase so で can mark it as the method.

1.3.n: Marks pressing the button as the way to launch the camera.

1.4.n: Signals surprise or excitement about the feature being introduced.

1.6.n: Used as a conversational beat during the demonstration, rather than an answer.

1.8.n: Refers to the camera app; its object marker を is left out in speech.

1.9.n: Casually emphasizes doing something in a single action, here one button press.

1.10.n: Combines with 一発 to express accomplishing something in one action.

1.11.n: 起動 plus する makes a verb for starting an app or device.

1.12.n: Turns 起動する into a noun-like phrase used in the ability pattern ことができる.

1.13.n: Marks the launching action as what is possible with できる.

1.14.n: In ことができる, expresses the ability to perform the preceding action.

1.15.n: Short for の; presents the camera-launching ability as an explanation.

1.16.n: Makes the explanation polite without changing the basic claim.

1.17.n: Emphasizes information the speaker is pointing out to the listener.

1.18.n: Softens the statement and invites the listener to share the speaker's reaction.

2.0.n: A conversational connector that moves on to the next feature.

2.2.n: Introduces an additional function of the same button.

2.3.n: Refers to the camera app; を is omitted before 開いて.

2.4.n: て-form of 開く; followed by から to show that opening happens first.

2.5.n: After a verb's て-form, marks an action completed before the next one.

2.6.n: Plain form before と, describing the action that triggers the result.

2.7.n: Marks a condition that predictably produces the following result.

2.9.n: Points back to the button being demonstrated, with its role left implicit in casual speech.

2.10.n: Used with 切る in the expression for taking a photo; を is omitted here.

2.11.n: In シャッターを切る, means triggering the shutter to take a photo, not physically cutting it.

2.12.n: Introduces the action being described before こと, packaging it as something the button can do.

2.13.n: Makes the preceding description into a noun-like phrase that can be followed by もできます.

2.14.n: Adds taking photos to the button's previously mentioned camera-launching function.

2.15.n: Polite form of できる, expressing that this additional action is possible.

3.0.n: Refers to the button and its functions as the topic of the speaker's evaluation.

3.1.n: Invites attention to the topic before the speaker gives an opinion.

3.3.n: With a positive description, suggests something is impressively or pleasantly so.

3.4.n: A な-adjective describing the feature as useful and easy to use.

3.5.n: Required after the な-adjective 便利 before the explanatory ん.

3.6.n: Short for の; gives the opinion an explanatory, conversational tone.

3.7.n: Keeps the statement polite despite its relaxed conversational style.

3.8.n: Adds emphasis to the speaker's positive assessment.

3.9.n: Invites agreement and softens the emphasis of よ.

0.lit: First, Camera Control. On this side, you know, beside the power button, this button exists, and…
0.tip: ありまして is a polite connecting form of ある, so the speaker is continuing rather than finishing the explanation.

1.lit: By pressing this, amazingly, yes, you can launch the camera in one shot, you know.
1.tip: Verb + ことで means by doing something, while verb + ことができる means can do something.

2.lit: And furthermore, after opening the camera, when you press, this can also do the act of releasing the shutter.
2.tip: て-form + から sets the order: open the camera first, then press the button.

3.lit: This, you know, is quite handy, you know.
3.tip: なかなか with a positive description means quite or impressively, not the difficulty suggested by なかなか with a negative verb.
